question: Which of the following is NOT taxable under the head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession?
options: A) Salary received by a partner from the firm, to the extent allowed to the firm
B) Sum received under a Keyman insurance policy
C) Rent from a house property owned by a trader, credited to his P&L account
D) Sum received for a non-compete agreement
explanation: Rent from a house property owned by the assessee is taxed under Income from House Property even if credited to the business P&L. A is 28(v), B is 28(vi), D is 28(va).

question: A partner's salary and interest received from the firm are taxable in his hands under the head:
options: C) Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
D) Exempt, as the firm has already paid tax
explanation: A partner is not an employee of the firm, so there is no employer-employee relationship and the Salaries head does not apply. Section 28(v) taxes it as business income, to the extent it was allowed to the firm under s. 40(b).

question: Ravi, a salaried employee, bought 2,000 kg of saffron once during the year intending to resell it at a profit, and did so. The profit is:
options: A) A capital gain, because it was a single transaction
B) Business income, as an adventure in the nature of trade
C) Exempt, being a casual receipt
explanation: Business under s. 2(13) includes any adventure in the nature of trade. An isolated purchase made with the intention of resale at a profit is business; continuity is not required. The intention at the time of purchase decides it.

question: Interest on the proprietor's own capital, debited to the P&L account, is:
options: C) Not allowed, being a notional expense
D) Allowed only if paid by cheque
explanation: A person cannot earn income from himself. Interest on own capital is notional and is added back. Contrast a firm, where interest to partners is allowed up to 12% under s. 40(b), because the firm and partner are separate assessees.

question: Explain any five incomes chargeable to tax under the head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession as per Section 28.
model_answer:
Section 28 charges the following, among others:

1. **28(i)** Profits and gains of any business or profession carried on by the assessee during the previous year.
2. **28(iv)** Value of any benefit or perquisite, whether convertible into money or not, arising from business or profession.
3. **28(v)** Interest, salary, bonus, commission or remuneration received by a partner from the firm, to the extent allowed to the firm under s. 40(b).
4. **28(va)** Any sum received under an agreement for not carrying out any activity in relation to a business (non-compete), or for not sharing know-how, patent, copyright or trademark.
5. **28(vi)** Any sum received under a Keyman insurance policy, including bonus.

Others acceptable: 28(ii) compensation on termination of management agency; 28(iii) income of trade associations from specific services to members; 28(iiia)-(iiie) export incentives; 28(via) FMV of inventory converted into capital asset.

marking_scheme.point: Profits of business/profession carried on during the PY — 28(i)
Any second valid clause with correct meaning
Any third valid clause with correct meaning
Any fourth valid clause with correct meaning
Any fifth valid clause with correct meaning (partner's remuneration must mention 'to the extent allowed u/s 40(b)')

question: The P&L account of Mr. Arjun, a trader, is credited with: (i) rent from a house property ₹60,000, (ii) dividend from an Indian company ₹8,000, (iii) profit on sale of an investment property ₹2,00,000, (iv) income-tax refund ₹5,000 with interest on refund ₹400, (v) agricultural income ₹30,000. State the correct treatment of each item while computing his business income, with reasons.
model_answer:
All five are **deducted** from the net profit, because none is business income:

| Item | Treatment | Head / reason |
|---|---|---|
| Rent ₹60,000 | Deduct | Taxed under Income from House Property |
| Dividend ₹8,000 | Deduct | Taxed under Income from Other Sources |
| Profit on sale of investment property ₹2,00,000 | Deduct | Capital asset, so taxed under Capital Gains (computed separately, not the book profit) |
| Income-tax refund ₹5,000 | Deduct | Not income at all, only a return of tax paid. Interest on refund ₹400 is taxable under IFOS |
| Agricultural income ₹30,000 | Deduct | Exempt u/s 10(1) |

marking_scheme.point: Rent deducted, taxable under House Property
Profit on investment property deducted, taxable as Capital Gains
Tax refund deducted as not income; interest on refund taxable under IFOS
